The statement’s emphasis on elevated inflation from pandemic-related imbalances and the Russia–Ukraine war is consistent with recent evidence that pandemic-driven shifts in consumption baskets and supply chains mechanically raised measured inflation (e.g., COVID-19 Inflation Weighting work). Inflation-at-risk research indicates a fat right tail for inflation outcomes in such environments, justifying a more forceful policy stance. Evidence on markups and profits suggests margin dynamics can amplify price pressures, reinforcing the need for vigilance. The 75 bp rate hike, higher administered rates (IORB/ON RRP), and balance sheet reduction align with modern implementation (Goodfriend) and Taylor-type reaction functions, and with the view that preventing monetary accommodation is key to avoiding persistent inflation (monetary vs. price inflation distinctions). Netting these, the communication remains hawkish with inflation risks still skewed to the upside despite robust employment, implying slightly more negative macro sentiment.
